The scalar polynomial certificate does not control nonlinear within-cell phase/sign variation, so the promised sharp logarithms, attaining families and oracle comparison remain open. tldr: Personalization can add no value even when treatment effects vary across individuals. The causal gain is benefit over the best single intervention, \(G=V-B\). In the stipulated binary observational model, a total whole-parent finite-sample honest interval and a lawful all-procedure original-record converse give supporting bounds with exponent \(d=\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\), separated by a factor \((\log n)^{2-d}\). Their constants are uniform in the moment coordinate, and the converse cutoff depends only on \(\alpha\). The entire null includes both one-sign cones, nonconstant effects and partial ties. Actual moment-class nesting makes both optima decrease as \(\nu\) increases. The proved smoothness-class nesting also shows that greater stipulated smoothness cannot worsen either optimum at any finite sample size. These orderings do not close the sharp logarithmic frontier or evaluate a sharp comparison across smoothness coordinates.
gap: Juditsky--Nemirovski leave a logarithmic cone gap in white noise, while Han--Jiao--Mukherjee leave the pointwise Hölder lower gap open. Neither gives \(J_0\) or \(J_0^{\mathrm k}\) for this original experiment. Li--Brunskill address a specified policy class under additional learning and noise conditions. The softmax manuscript of Whitehouse et al. already motivates the same gain, while its asymptotic inference requires controlled nonzero-gap density, bounded outcomes and nuisance-rate premises.
